BLOCKED ON RIGHTS -- no __items.csv written. The instrument is the Spanish UWES-17 (Encuesta de Bienestar y Trabajo). The paper's Measures section states only "we used a Spanish version of the Utrecht Work Engagement Scale (UWES-17) [47]", and reference 47 is Schaufeli & Bakker, Work Engagement Scale, Preliminary Manual, Occupational Health Psychology Unit, Utrecht University -- i.e. the rights holders' own manual is the cited and only source of the administered wording. That manual prints the 17-item Spanish work version on pp.54-55 and carries, immediately beneath it and on every other instrument page, the clause: "(c) Schaufeli & Bakker (2003). The Utrecht Work Engagement Scale is free for use for non-commercial scientific research. Commercial and/or non-scientific use is prohibited, unless previous written permission is granted by the authors." (Test_manual_UWES_English.pdf v1.1 Dec 2004, retrieved 2026-09-04 from wilmarschaufeli.nl/publications/Schaufeli/Test%20Manuals/; the Spanish student version on p.56 carries the same clause under Schaufeli, Salanova & Bakker 2003.) That is a quotable, rights-holder-stated non-commercial restriction on the item wording, so the itemtext_standard.md 2026-09-04 ruling (irw#1891) fires exactly as written: write no items CSV, record blocked, quote the clause. WHY THE ECR-R SOURCE-LICENCE CARVE-OUT DOES NOT RESCUE IT: that ruling says the licence of the source IRW actually copied from governs, so an instrument author's NC statement cannot narrow what an openly licensed publication published. Here there is no such publication to copy from. The study's CC BY 4.0 deposit is a single XLSX (S1 File, 10.1371/journal.pone.0197276.s001, sheet Hoja1, 210x89) whose UWES block, columns 32-48, is headed only "Item 1" ... "Item 17" with a VIG/DED/ABS subscale tag -- zero item wording -- and the article body reproduces exactly ONE of the 17 items as an illustration ("I find the work that I do full of meaning and purpose", = manual item 2, DE1). This is the chinvararak_2021_ecr / de_vries_2022_hexaco_* shape (the only publication of the wording is restricted), not the ECR-R shape. THE MAPPING IS FULLY ESTABLISHED, recorded so an unblock is cheap and needs no re-investigation. data/dominguez_2018_job_crafting.py assigns item_1..item_17 positionally to XLSX columns 32..48; those columns are headed "Item 1".."Item 17" in the sheet's own header row, and every live per-item mean and n reproduces its source column exactly (max |diff| = 0.00e+00 over 17 items, n = 202 each; the same comparison shifted one column left misses by up to 1.14). The sheet's own subscale row tags cols 32-48 VIG DED ABS VIG DED ABS DED VIG ABS DED ABS VIG DED ABS VIG ABS VIG, which equals the canonical UWES-17 assignment (vigour 1,4,8,12,15,17; dedication 2,5,7,10,13; absorption 3,6,9,11,14,16) at 17/17 positions -- so item_N is the manual's printed item N, and the one item the paper does quote lands on item_2 as it should. Response anchors were also fully recoverable and are NOT the blocked part: the sheet's own row-0 header gives them verbatim in English ("0: Never 1: Almost never (A few times a year or less) 2: Rarely (once a month or less) 3: Sometimes (A few times a month) 4: Often (once a week) 5: Very often ( A few times a week) 6: Always (Every day)"), matching the live resp set {0,...,6}. They were not shipped alone: per the option-only rule (irw#1770) a generic 0-6 Never..Always ladder carries no item referent, and unlike estevez_2021 the stems here are determinately barred rather than one hop away, so a fixes/ park would never be completed. Step 3b instrument check: no mismatch. Live ground truth via irw_table_sets (no export): 3,434 rows, 17 items, resp {0,1,2,3,4,5,6}, n = 202 per item -- consistent with the UWES-17 on its published 0-6 scale, and the sibling scales in the same file (JCS 21 items 1-5, MBI 22 items 0-6, ITL 3 items 1-5) are separate tables. RETRY TEST: NO. A determinate verdict was reached, not an access failure -- every source needed was retrieved successfully (PLOS article HTML, the S1 File XLSX, the UWES Preliminary Manual PDF). It would flip only if (a) Schaufeli & Bakker relicensed the UWES or granted IRW written permission, (b) an openly licensed (non-NC) publication reproducing the full Spanish UWES-17 wording turned up and Ben accepted it under the ECR-R source-licence rule, or (c) Ben ruled that this clause is not the kind of non-commercial restriction irw#1891 was about. ESCALATION: this rule reaches the whole UWES family. Two UWES tables already shipped under the pre-ruling regime and have never been audited against it -- algner2022_uwes (batch_003, uploaded 2026-08-17, text_source=canonical_instrument, wording taken from the official German UWES-9 PDF on wilmarschaufeli.nl, i.e. the same NC-clause source) and baka2023_uwes (batch_007, uploaded 2026-08-18, Polish UWES-17 taken from the study's own CC BY figshare .sav variable labels, which is the ECR-R shape and may well survive). The sibling table dominguez_2018_mbi in this same paper is the MBI-HSS, a Mind Garden commercial instrument, and is likely to hit the fee-licence rule; dominguez_2018_jcs (Dutch Job Crafting Scale) and dominguez_2018_itl are not affected by this clause.

BLOCKED ON RIGHTS -- no __items.csv written. The instrument is the 8-item Short Grit Scale (Grit-S; Duckworth & Quinn, 2009), of which this table holds items 1, 3 and 5 (live item codes grit_1/grit_3/grit_5; source columns Q19_1/Q19_2/Q19_3, labelled SGS_1/SGS_3/SGS_5 in the deposit's own scale-number row). The rights holder is Angela Duckworth's lab, which publishes the only authoritative copies of the 8- and 12-item Grit Scales at angeladuckworth.com/measures and states there, verbatim: "Researchers and educators are welcome to use the scales developed by Angela's lab for non-commercial purposes" and "These scales are copyrighted. They cannot be published or used for commercial purposes or wide public distribution. Journalists and book authors should not reproduce these scales or any part of them." That is a non-commercial clause AND an explicit bar on publication and wide distribution, so it fires the SKILL's rights rules twice: the TIMSS NC rule, and the 2026-09-04 DSES no-redistribution ruling under which a quotable restriction on the rights holder's own copy overrides the licence of the deposit IRW copied from. It does override one here: the response data came from a CC0 Harvard Dataverse deposit (doi:10.7910/DVN/Y75CP2) whose xlsx prints the three item stems in a 'Question' row, so under the ECR-R source-licence rule alone this table would have shipped. Shipping item text IS publishing the scale to wide public distribution, which is exactly what the clause forbids. NOT a data problem: the mapping was checked anyway and is exact -- all 15 item x resp cell counts in the live table equal those of the assigned raw column (grit_1 28/64/144/56/6, grit_3 18/65/100/98/17, grit_5 11/39/87/123/38), and none of the 5 wrong permutations matches, so the withheld mapping was verified; see verify_dpt_noncog__grit.R. RETRY TEST: NO -- an unchanged retry now cannot produce a different result. The source is located, open, and prints the wording; the block is a determinate rights verdict. It would flip only if Duckworth's lab changed or waived those terms, or if Ben ruled that this particular clause does not govern a CC0 deposit's own printing of the items. SCOPE: this is an instrument-level ruling about Duckworth-lab scales, not about this study -- the same block would hit the pending table grit_BrummerHoffman_2021 and any other Grit-S/Grit-O table. It does NOT extend to this study's siblings, which are other authors' instruments (Schutte SREIT, Davis IRI, IUS, MSI, PFQ) with their own separate terms.
